newsitem.title: UK: UK's ITC says satellite broadcaster broke codes.
newsitem.headline: UK's ITC says satellite broadcaster broke codes.

text.p: Britain's commercial television watchdog on Friday said it has warned a UK-based satellite television broadcaster that it must comply with UK television codes governing programme standards, even for programmes not intended for British viewers.

The Independent Television Commission (ITC) said it issued a formal warning to TV3 Broadcasting Group Ltd for serious breaches of ITC codes concerning sponsor credits and influence, competitions and product references related to its programme "IQ Lotto".

"IQ Lotto", supplied by a TV3 Group's Comviq unit and broadcast on TV3 Sweden, offered prizes of Nokia mobile phones and paid-for talk time with Comviq. Contestants entered the lottery by sending in weekly telephone call invoices. The programme also included numerous visual and verbal references to Nokia phones, the ITC said.
TV3 Sweden has apologised and removed the series, the ITC said.
The ITC also said it found that two programmes broadcast by TV3 Denmark in a series featuring comedians Finn and Jacob gave undue prominence to the brewer Tuborg and its Tuborg Squash beverage.

The ITC noted that Finn and Jacob have both appeared in adverts for Tuborg Squash in Denmark and the programme included out-takes from these ads as well as numerous verbal and visual references to Tuborg.
